summary: Strongly bullish momentum following a powerful dual catalyst day on Aug 12: (1) July CPI came in cooler than expected at 2.7% YoY headline (vs 2.8% expected), cementing September rate cut expectations to ~90% probability, and (2) US-China tariff truce extended 90 days to Nov 10, avoiding escalation from 30% to 145%. S&P 500 closed at record 6,445.76 (+1.13%), Nasdaq at record 21,681.90 (+1.39%), Dow +483 pts to 44,458.61. All 11 sectors closed green. Aug 13 is a continuation/digestion day — Dow jumped another 450+ pts, S&P and Nasdaq logged back-to-back records (up ~0.3% and ~0.1% respectively). Key risk: PPI data on Aug 14 could reverse sentiment if hot. Oil bearish (EIA forecast sub-$60 by Q4, OPEC+ unwinding cuts). Gold near record highs ~$3,488. 10Y yield fell 4bps to 4.25%. Treasury Secretary Bessent called for 150-175bps of cuts. Small caps (Russell 2000) surging on rate sensitivity — up 2.9% in August, 7.3% for the full month. CoreWeave -18% on guidance cut is a notable AI infrastructure crack.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.content: US-China tariff truce extended 90 days on Aug 11-12, keeping tariffs at 30% on Chinese imports (vs potential 145% escalation). This was a major relief rally catalyst alongside CPI. Trump-Putin Alaska summit scheduled for Aug 15 regarding Ukraine — Trump dropped ceasefire demand in favor of 'Peace Agreement' approach. European leaders cautious. Defense spending remains elevated globally — Elbit Systems reporting 21% YoY revenue growth driven by Israel/NATO demand. Geopolitical risk temporarily suppressed but not resolved.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: July CPI released Aug 12: headline +0.2% MoM / +2.7% YoY (below 2.8% consensus). Core CPI +0.3% MoM / +3.1% YoY (in-line, but accelerating from 2.9% in June — fastest since Feb). Tariff impact visible in household furnishings (+0.7% MoM), core commodities inflation (+1.2% YoY, fastest in 2+ years). Fed rate cut expectations surged: September cut fully priced (~90%), October cut probability jumped to 67%. Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly called for 150-175bps of total cuts. 10Y yield fell to 4.25%, 2Y fell to 3.73%. PPI due Aug 14 — the next inflection point. S&P 500 Q2 earnings: 83% beat rate, +10.6% YoY aggregate operating earnings. GDP strong. Unemployment low but moderating.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Key Aug 13 earnings: Brinker International (EAT) blowout Q4 — comp sales +21.3%, Chili's +23.7%, revenue $1.45B vs $1.20B PY, $400M buyback. Elbit Systems (ESLT) Q2 — revenues +21% YoY, EPS +55%. Performance Food Group (PFGC) FY2025 record $63B revenue, EBITDA +19.9%, US Foods merger inquiry disclosed. Global-e Online (GLBE) Q2 revenue +28% to $214.9M, first GAAP profitability. CAVA cut same-store guidance to 4-6% from 6-8%, stock -16.6%. CoreWeave (CRWV) -18% on guidance cut. Paramount Skydance (PSKY) +37% on $7.7B UFC deal momentum. Apple jumped on Bloomberg AI comeback report. Circle IPO priced above range at $37. Hudbay Minerals (HBM) strong Q2 with significant free cash flow.

sections.title: TechAI
sections.content: AI infrastructure spending massive but cracks emerging. CoreWeave cut 2025 revenue guidance ($5.15-5.35B to $5.05-5.15B) due to third-party data center delays — stock -18%, signaling execution risk. Hyperscaler capex (MSFT, GOOG, AMZN, META) remains robust. Nvidia Blackwell ramp strong, approaching $50B data center revenue quarter. AMD inked OpenAI deal. SOX index +34.5% YTD. Apple announced ambitious AI product roadmap Aug 13 (Bloomberg): tabletop robot (2027), smart speaker with display (2026), lifelike Siri. Analog semiconductor super-cycle gaining momentum — ADI and peers surging. 50% copper tariff benefits domestic chip supply chain.

sections.title: Energy
sections.content: Bearish oil setup dominates. EIA Aug 12 STEO forecasts Brent below $60/bbl by Q4 2025, averaging ~$50 in 2026. OPEC+ unwinding 2.2mb/d voluntary cuts by September — a year ahead of schedule. WTI in low-to-mid $60s. US production at all-time high near 13.6mb/d. Oil fell 1.6% on Aug 13. Supply glut building. Gold near record highs ~$3,488/oz, benefiting from rate cut expectations and geopolitical hedging. Copper volatile after 50% tariff — two-tier market benefits FCX (domestic), hurts SCCO (importer).

sections.title: Policy
sections.content: Five major policy threads: (1) Trump's 50% copper import tariff effective Aug 1 — creates winners/losers. (2) US-China 90-day tariff extension signed Aug 11 — prevents escalation, markets rallied. Average effective tariff rate at 10.55%, China at 39.2%. (3) CMS Medicare Advantage rate guidance pressuring managed care stocks. (4) Treasury Sec Bessent publicly pushing for 150-175bps of total cuts — unusually aggressive political pressure on Fed. (5) Trump-Putin Alaska summit Aug 15 could move defense/energy. Core commodities inflation accelerating (+1.2% YoY), suggesting tariff passthrough happening but controlled.

scenarios.trade: EAT reported one of the strongest restaurant quarters in years on Aug 13 pre-market. Traffic-driven growth (+16% Chili's traffic) is the highest-quality comp driver — not just pricing. 2-year sales growth of +39% shows sustainable momentum. $400M buyback provides EPS support floor. In a market where rate cut expectations boost consumer discretionary and all 11 sectors closed green the prior day, a company demonstrating genuine traffic growth commands premium multiple expansion. The Dow gained another 450+ pts on Aug 13, providing strong market tailwind.

scenarios.implication: Stock may gap up beyond optimal entry after earnings. Restaurant comps face increasingly difficult comparisons. Tariff-driven food cost inflation (household furnishings +0.7% MoM in CPI) could eventually pressure restaurant input costs. Consumer spending deceleration risk if labor market weakens.

scenarios.trade: CoreWeave's guidance cut is the first major crack in the AI infrastructure narrative. For a stock priced for flawless execution, even a modest trim framed as 'timing shift' destroyed confidence. Third-party construction delays suggest systemic capacity constraint issues, not company-specific. The broad market rally actually makes CRWV's underperformance more painful — investors rotating to higher-conviction names. Stock eventually fell 50%+ from highs over subsequent months. Institutional selling continues for days after a guidance cut of this magnitude on a recently-IPO'd name.

scenarios.implication: Short squeeze risk if hyperscaler announces expanded contract. AI narrative could lift all boats in risk-on tape. Stock may find technical support after 18% drop. Contracted backlog ($56B) provides fundamental floor. Broad market strength could trigger short covering.

scenarios.trade: When a high-multiple fast-casual darling cuts same-store guidance for the first time, the de-rating is typically multi-day as growth fund managers exit positions. SSS of 2.1% vs 6-8% guidance range represents dramatic deceleration that questions the entire growth thesis. The stock traded at extreme premium to restaurant peers, making downside asymmetric. Even after 16.6% drop, likely hasn't fully repriced to new growth trajectory. Analyst downgrades follow over 1-3 days. After-hours recovery to $84.50 may provide short entry on Aug 13 open.

scenarios.implication: Stock may be oversold near-term after 16.6% drop. Maintained margin guidance shows cost discipline. Restaurant opening guidance raised to 68-70, preserving unit growth story. Broad market strength provides support. Some after-hours buying at $84.50 suggests floor forming.

scenarios.trade: Dual catalyst of cooler CPI + US-China trade truce creates ideal small-cap environment. Small caps are more rate-sensitive (higher leverage = more benefit from lower borrowing costs), more domestically focused (trade truce reduces uncertainty), and more economically sensitive (rate cuts signal easier financial conditions). Russell 2000 surged 7.3% in August — best monthly performance of the year. Rotation from mega-cap tech to small caps is multi-week theme. Bessent calling for 150-175bps provides political tailwind. If PPI soft tomorrow, theme accelerates.

scenarios.implication: Hot PPI on Aug 14 could crush rate-cut expectations and small caps. Higher beta both ways — reversal would be painful. Russell 2000 P/E at 16.3x already above average. Trade truce is 90-day extension, not resolution. CoreWeave type cracks could spread risk-off sentiment.

scenarios.trade: UFC deal is transformative — secures most valuable live sports content in fastest-growing demo (18-34). Elimination of PPV in favor of Paramount+ subscription drives massive subscriber adds. Stock's 37% surge reflects initial re-rating but deal's long-term value changes Paramount+ value proposition fundamentally. Post-Skydance merger execution being validated by management's aggressive content strategy. In streaming wars, content-rich platforms win. Momentum continuation likely as analyst upgrades flow.

scenarios.implication: Already +37% — chasing risk at the top. UFC deal is expensive ($7.7B) and may pressure margins before subscriber revenue materializes. Skydance merger integration risk ongoing. Low-price stocks have gap risk. Volume may thin after initial surge.

scenarios.trade: Energy is worst-positioned sector. Bearish confluence: OPEC+ abandoning production discipline a year early, US production at all-time highs, EIA forecasting sub-$60 oil by Q4, growing global inventories. CPI-driven rally in other sectors makes energy's relative underperformance stark — money rotating OUT of energy into rate-sensitive plays. WTI in low $60s pressuring E&P margins. Fresh EIA forecast (released Aug 12) is institutional intelligence driving selling. If PPI soft tomorrow, rate-cut narrative strengthens further — bearish for commodities.

scenarios.implication: Geopolitical escalation (Ukraine summit Aug 15, Middle East) could spike oil overnight. OPEC+ could reverse production increase. Hot PPI could strengthen commodities. Energy stocks may already price in lower oil. Short covering rallies possible in broad risk-on tape.

Freeport-McMoRan primary beneficiary of 50% copper tariff. Morgan Stanley upgrade Aug 11. But copper market volatile and tariff exemptions for cathodes complicate. Watch copper price action for entry.
Global-e Q2 revenue +28%, first GAAP profitability. Cross-border ecommerce benefits from tariff complexity. Post-earnings move may be priced in. Watch for breakout confirmation.
Elbit Systems Q2 blowout (revenue +21%, EPS +55%). Defense secular growth. Stock may gap up beyond optimal entry. Watch for pullback.
SPDR Regional Banking ETF. Rate cut expectations are strongest tailwind for regional banks (NIM expansion). Monitor for sustained rotation confirmation before entry.
